name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: Mayon, Kīlauea active; no red codes
summary: Mayon keeps emitting ash and Kīlauea fountains again; no red aviation codes on major air routes
state: Mayon in the Philippines emitted ash again in early November, with VAAC advisories issued on 3 Nov (GMA News; VolcanoDiscovery). Kīlauea's episode 56 of lava fountaining ended after nearly six hours on 6 Nov, a recurring pattern with no major ash threat to aviation (The Watchers). No volcano near major international air routes was at aviation colour code red and no large explosive eruption was reported as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Flights in the Bicol region of the Philippines can be disrupted by Mayon ash at short notice. Check with your airline, and follow PHIVOLCS guidance if you are near the volcano.
rubric_hit: No aviation colour code red near major routes and no large eruption (Normal)

sources.title: GMA News — Mayon Volcano emits ash anew

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.
